title: compact reservation merger and jitter-tolerant burst controller
author: Arjun Patel
description:
Motivation: Reservation fragmentation from many small tenant commitments results in underutilized GPU slots and higher unit costs for Dedicated. This PR introduces a compact reservation coalescer that opportunistically merges adjacent low-utilization reservations into compact buckets without violating per-tenant throughput guarantees and a jitter-tolerant burst controller that smooths microbursts to reduce transient allocation churn.

Summary of changes: Add a new controller (ReservationCoalescer) that periodically scans per-pool reservation timelines, identifies candidates for safe coalescing using a time-windowed overlap heuristic and a safety headroom check, and performs transactional merge operations with undoable checkpoints. Introduce BurstHedger which applies randomized holdback windows and proportional token dampening to spread microbursts slightly in time to avoid synchronized allocation spikes. Add telemetry (HDR sketches for occupancy_histogram, counters for coalesce_ops, hedger_backpressure_events, and per-tenant headroom_reserve_bytes). Add canary rollout config and an operator flag to enable conservative mode.

Checklist: - [x] reservation reconciliation loop and coalescer reconciler - [x] safe merge transaction with rollback path - [x] jitter-tolerant burst hedger implementation - [x] metrics and tracing spans - [x] unit tests for merge/rollback and hedger token logic - [x] e2e scenario and load runner job - [x] docs: ops runbook and configuration guide

Backward compatibility & safety: Coalescer is behind a feature flag and defaults to disabled for existing clusters. Merge transactions are guarded by a conservative safety check: min-utilization threshold, per-tenant throughput budget checks, and a 5-minute observation window before any irreversible changes in non-conservative mode. BurstHedger is opt-in per-pool and exposes tuning knobs for holdback_ms and randomized_jitter_pct.

Why different from prior autoscaler work: This PR focuses on reducing fragmentation at the reservation layer (not autoscaling thresholds) and on microburst smoothing at the request admission layer rather than large-scale rebalance — the net effect is fewer short-lived allocations and lower scheduler thrash under bursty multi-tenant patterns.

How to test: unit tests simulate race between create/delete and coalescer to assert no lost reservations; e2e uses a synthetic mix of 1000 small reservations across 50 pools with bursts to validate correctness and measure cost impact.

Maya Chen: This looks promising, the merge transaction shape is the key risk. Please add more comments on the undo path and an instrumentation span for the merge critical section.

Arjun Patel: Added explicit 'merge-undo' span and comments in the reconciler; clarified txn boundaries and persisted checkpoint structure in the runbook.

release_notes:
Enableable feature: reservation coalescer and burst hedger. When enabled the platform may reduce total reserved GPU footprint by coalescing small low-util reservations; conservative defaults are safe. Operators must monitor reservation_coalescer.coalesce_ops and hedger_backpressure_events. Soak plan: enable in 5% of pools for 24h, then 25% for 48h, then full rollout.
Observed perf: synthetic load showed ~6.5% reduction in reserved GPU-hours at steady-state and a 7% decrease in scheduling churn. Median generation latency impact <2ms, p95 unchanged, p99 reduced by ~40ms in noisy microburst scenarios.
testing_notes: Unit tests added for merge semantics and rollback. E2E scenario simulates 1k small reservations across 50 pools with synthetic bursts; loadrunner script included under tests/e2e. Bench harness run on staging cluster 'dedicated-stg-3' for 6h. CI initially failed on TestReservationMergeRace due to race; fixed by serializing index updates. All CI checks passed on second run.
perf_results: Staging run (dedicated-stg-3) with mixed-tenancy workload: reserved GPU-hours down 6.5% over 6h window, avg scheduler rebinds per-minute down 12%, tail scheduling latency (p99) decreased 40ms during burst windows. Cost projection: estimated 4.8% monthly infra cost saving for clusters with >=25% small reservations.
notes: Operator knobs: --enable-reservation-coalescer, --coalesce-min-util=0.12, --coalesce-window=5m, per-pool hedger config under charts. Follow runbook in docs/ops/reservation-coalescer-runbook.md before enabling in production.
